pill.desc: clear to slightly opalescent, colorless to pale brown solution in a single-dose vial

tell: A CD20-directed antibody given every 6 months, with no boxed warning.

clues.text: Cleared principally by catabolism, and its metabolism has not been directly studied. Mild renal or hepatic impairment does not change its pharmacokinetics.
A recombinant humanized protein with a glycosylated structure and a molecular mass of approximately 145 kDa.
Approved under a BLA as 300 mg/10 mL single-dose vials, dosed as 600 mg every 6 months.
No boxed warning. Contraindicated with active hepatitis B infection and after a life-threatening infusion reaction; upper respiratory tract infections and infusion reactions are most common.
Relapsing forms of MS and primary progressive MS in adults, and relapsing-remitting MS in children 10 years and older weighing 25 kg or more.
Binds CD20, a surface antigen on pre-B and mature B lymphocytes, causing antibody-dependent cytolysis and complement-mediated lysis.
The generic name begins with O and has eleven letters.
